blocks.text: Good morning Jennifer,

Picking up from Michael's note on Friday, here is where the messaging framework for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} stands this morning. The revised version is in the shared folder, saved under today's date.

Three things have changed. The opening narrative is now three sentences long. The growth section comes ahead of the margin section. And every financial proof point is highlighted in yellow for your team to confirm.

The proof points are the one part we cannot settle on our own. We want each figure the executives cite to be one your finance team is happy to stand behind. Could you mark which ones to keep and which to drop? A short reply is plenty.
Once we have your marks, I will turn the talking points around the same day. Let me know if you want me to take another pass on the framework before then.
Regards
Hi Jennifer,

John's revised framework is the version we would like to put in front of the {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} executives, and since the proof points he highlighted on Monday are now the only open question on it, I want to set out exactly what we need from your side so that the drafting does not stall while each of us waits on the other.

1. A keep or drop on each highlighted proof point, and for any you drop, the figure your finance team would prefer the executives use instead, if there is one.
2. The name of the person on your side who gives final sign-off on anything the executives will say to investors, so that we know whose approval closes each draft.
3. A two-hour slot in the last week of the month for a working session with you, John, Amy and me, where we go through the talking points and the investor questions line by line against the confirmed figures.
If the first item is quicker to settle by phone than in writing, I can take a call at any point this afternoon, and John can join and make the changes while we talk.
Sincerely
Good morning Jennifer,
Following Michael's list this morning, I have tried to make the first item quicker for you to answer.

The highlighted proof points are now on a single page, in the order they appear in the framework. Each one has a keep or drop column beside it, with room for a replacement figure. The page is in the shared {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} folder, next to the framework.

On the third item, Amy and I can make any slot in the last week of the month. Amy will bring her first draft of the investor questions and answers. That way we can test the answers against the same confirmed figures in the same session.
As soon as you pick a time, I will send a calendar hold to everyone on this thread.
Regards
Hi Jennifer,

Ahead of the working session, and with John's one-page list of proof points now in the folder alongside the framework, I would like to agree the order we take things in on the day, so that the two hours go to the questions that need you in the room and the drafts themselves can be read beforehand.

1. Proof points: your marks on John's list, and any replacement figures, so that the framework is final for drafting purposes.
2. Talking points: the CEO and CFO talking points read aloud against the framework, marking anything that does not sound like the way either of them actually speaks.
3. Investor questions: Amy's first draft of the questions and answers, starting with outlook, since those are the questions most likely to come up and the hardest to answer consistently.
4. Approval route: who signs off on each kind of material at {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} and how long a round normally takes, so that we can plan the rest of the drafting around it.
If there is anything you would add to that list, or a question you already know is on the executives' minds, send it over before the session and we will take it first.
Sincerely
Working Session Minutes: {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} Executive Messaging

This was the working session set up in the email thread earlier this month, held to settle the open items on the messaging framework, the executive talking points and the investor questions and answers before the next round of drafts goes to the {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} executives, and it followed the four-item order agreed by email beforehand.
Present

items: Michael Morris, Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
John Macias, Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Amy Carter, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: What was discussed
1. Proof points

Jennifer Herrera brought her marks on the one-page list of proof points, and the group took them in the order they appear in the framework. Most were kept as written. Where finance was not comfortable with a figure, it was taken out and not replaced, because the executives should not cite any number they would struggle to explain if an investor asked a follow-up question. With those marks the framework is final for drafting purposes, and any later change to a figure will come through Jennifer, so that the framework, the talking points and the questions and answers are always updated together.
2. Talking points

John Macias read both sets of talking points aloud against the agreed framework. The CFO's points are close to final, but the group agreed they should open with the figures and then explain them, which is the reverse of the current draft. The CEO's points read as though they were written for the page and not for speaking, particularly in the opening section, and the second half of the growth section repeats the framework almost word for word, so John will shorten the sentences throughout and cut that passage.
3. Investor questions

Amy Carter took the group through her first draft of the questions and answers, starting with outlook as agreed. Jennifer Herrera asked that any answer touching on outlook use only language that finance has already approved for outside use and go no further than it, and Amy will check every outlook answer against that language before the second draft goes out. Two subjects came up in discussion that the draft does not yet cover, use of cash and hiring plans, and Amy will add questions on both.
4. Approval route

Jennifer Herrera will be the single route for approvals on the client side: she will collect sign-off from the executives and from counsel and send back one consolidated set of comments on each draft. She asked for about a working week for each round, so that no one on her side is asked to turn a draft around overnight, and the team agreed to plan the remaining drafting on that basis, with one round open at a time.
Actions agreed

rows: Circulate the final messaging framework with the agreed proof points
Shorten the CEO talking points and cut the repeated growth passage; reorder the CFO talking points to open with the figures
In time for the next approval round
Check every outlook answer against approved language and add questions on use of cash and hiring plans
Second draft to Jennifer Herrera within a week
Collect executive and counsel sign-off on the framework and return consolidated comments
About a working week from receipt
Propose a format and timing for rehearsal sessions with the executives
Once the second round of comments is back

blocks.text: Corrections to these minutes should come to Michael Morris, and once any are in, the minutes will go to everyone who attended along with the final framework.
Status Report: Executive Messaging for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}
Where the work stands

We are about halfway through the engagement, and the work is on plan. The messaging framework is final. The talking points and the investor questions and answers are both in their second drafts, and both drafts are with your office for comment. Nothing has slipped so far. The scope has not changed.
This report covers three things. First, what we have finished. Second, what comes next. Third, the risks we are watching and what we are doing about each one. The budget position follows at the end.
Finished so far
Five pieces of work are complete or have reached an agreed second draft. In order:

items: Messaging framework. Signed off by the executives and counsel, with every proof point confirmed by your finance team. Figures finance did not want cited were removed, not reworded.
Approval route. Approvals on your side now run through one point of contact, who collects sign-off from the executives and from counsel. Each round comes back to us as one set of comments.

Working session. We went through the framework, the talking points and the investor questions line by line. The minutes record each decision and each action. Every action from that session is done, apart from the rehearsal plan, which waits on your comments on the second drafts.
Talking points, second draft. The CEO's points are shorter and easier to say aloud, and the repeated growth passage is gone. The CFO's points now open with the figures and then explain them.

Investor questions and answers, second draft. Amy Carter checked every outlook answer against language finance has approved for outside use. She also added questions on use of cash and on hiring plans.

blocks.text: The first half has gone smoothly, and much of that is down to how quickly your team turned the proof points around. Settling the figures early meant every later draft could be checked against one agreed list. We will keep working that way.
Ahead of us

The second half of the engagement moves from drafting to delivery. Until now the question has been whether the words are right. From here it is whether they hold up when the executives say them under questioning. Four pieces of work remain:

items: Comments on the second drafts. We will fold in your consolidated comments as soon as they arrive. We will keep to one round open at a time, as agreed.

Rehearsal sessions. Michael Morris will lead them, with Amy and me asking the questions an investor would ask. The aim is to find any answer that does not yet hold up while there is still time to fix it.
Reactive lines. We will draft short, approved answers for the questions we hope will not come up. Each one will rest on a confirmed figure or on approved language, and on nothing else.
Final package. One document holding the framework, both sets of talking points and the questions and answers, in the form the executives will carry with them.

blocks.text: We expect the rehearsals to produce more changes than anything else left in the plan. That is normal. A question that looks easy on paper often needs a shorter, plainer answer once someone has to say it out loud. We have left time for a further round on the questions and answers after rehearsal.
Risks we are watching
Each of these is manageable at present, and none needs a decision from you today. We list them so that nothing comes as a surprise.

items: Executive calendars. Rehearsals only work if both executives can attend. We would like to fix the sessions soon, before their calendars fill.
Changing figures. When the current quarter closes, some proof points may move. We will refresh them with finance before rehearsals, so that no one practices with an old number.
Approval timing. A round takes about a working week on your side. That works well at present. It would become tight if two rounds overlapped, which is why we keep to one at a time.
Scope. Requests for related material, such as a board version of the narrative, are welcome. We will flag any request that falls outside the agreed scope before we start on it.

blocks.text: Budget

The engagement fee is {{fact:f:E-2023-001.fee}}, as set out in the engagement letter. Work to date is in line with it. We expect to complete the remaining scope within that fee, and we will tell you early if anything changes our view. There have been no requests outside the agreed scope so far, so no change to the fee has been discussed.
One request

Rehearsals are the next milestone, and they depend on the executives' time. So our one request this period is for two rehearsal windows from the {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} executive offices. Once we have them, Michael Morris will confirm the format, and I will send the materials to each executive a few days ahead.
